setlist_extra.title: That's It For The Other One

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Viola Lee Blues** (3 reviews): This Viola Lee is a very long, extremely intense jam of enormous power, best played loudly; Reviewer calls this the best Viola Lee on tape, beating every other version he has heard, including King's Beach Bowl [6][11][13]
- **The Other One** (1 other source): Last show with one of the early Other One lyric sets, including the line about the head not being in sight [2]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (1 review): Cryptical is very spacey; Bobby's timing on the 'Coming around' line is funky, and the lyrics are of their era [10]
- **Viola Lee Blues Feedback** (1 review): Feedback follows Viola Lee, reviewer guesses, because the guitars would be badly out of tune after the meltdown [11]
- **Good Morning, Little Schoolgirl** (1 other source): The circulating version is actually from 02/03/68, spliced in by David Gans to replace the 02/02 version for GDH 310 [2]

## Setlist highlights

- **Clementine**: rare: 7 archived performances [16]
- **Born Cross-Eyed**: rare: 14 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1968-02-02.sbd.jools.20299.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 7 songs; 33 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd68-02-02.sbd.jools.15801.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 6 songs; 46 min; rated 4.62/5 by 37 [2]. Said about its sound: Tape quality is rough, but the reviewer still thinks it sounds great; The Other One is nearly in perfect pitch, as one listener found by playing guitar along; levels are powerful [5][12]
- **gd1968-02-02.sbd.miller.97345.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 4 songs; 33 min; rated 3.93/5 by 14 [3]

## Around the show

- The Crystal Ballroom is an old theater with a huge spring-loaded dance floor and a wonderful atmosphere [4]
- Joe Jupille's newspaper research found ads only for Quicksilver and the Dead at Eagles Auditorium on 1/26 and 1/27 [1]
- Captures the band turned fully psychedelic, but before the later DS>SS>11>LL sequence; reviewer ranks it with the next night's show [4]
- Reviewer says this Viola Lee is unlike the 1973 and 1977 versions [6]
- It lacks the special occasion of the Haight Street Viola Lee, but reviewer still ranks it higher [11]
- Shows from this run were used on Anthem of the Sun; here the music is heard in plainer, unprocessed form [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1968-02-02.sbd.jools.20299.sbeok.shnf**: This show circulates mislabeled as 1/23/68 Eagles Auditorium, though no documents show Eagles shows on that date [1]
- **gd68-02-02.sbd.jools.15801.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Julian (Jools) Elliott; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Gans aired this show and 2/3/68 on The Grateful Dead Hour soon after they surfaced [7]
- **gd1968-02-02.sbd.miller.97345.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> (4 Track) Master Reels -> Dat (44.1k) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by George Hunter: [Grateful Dead Quicksilver NOTICE! 1968 Crystal Ballroom AOR 3.103 Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/374636/Grateful-Dead-Quicksilver-NOTICE-1968-Crystal-Ballroom-AOR-3103-Concert-Poster) [17]
- Fan art by jeffersonboots.free.fr: [Grateful Dead](http://jeffersonboots.free.fr/dead/dead.htm) [18]
